summary: Tianshu Zhu specializes in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. She earned an MA from Northwest University and a PhD from Ohio State University under John C. Huntington. In 2007, she became an Associate Professor at the University of Macau.

Tilak Kariyawasam is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He served as head of the Department of Pali and Buddhist Studies at the University of Kelaniya (attested 1993) and Dean of the Graduate School at the International Buddhist College (attested 2014).

Tilmann Vetter (1937–2012) worked in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He completed his PhD at the University of Vienna under Erich Frauwallner and Erich Heintel, later serving as professor at Leiden University from around 1976 to 2002.

Timothy Dubber is an Indology and history/archaeology scholar. He earned degrees from the University of New South Wales Canberra and the University of Edinburgh. He became an Australian National University PhD candidate in 2025 and a UNSW Adjunct Fellow in 2026.

Timothy Hugh Barrett is a scholar of Sinology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He studied at the University of Cambridge and Yale University. He taught at Cambridge (attested 1981) and became a professor at SOAS University of London in 1986.

Timothy Lenz works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed graduate studies at the University of Washington under Richard G. Salomon and Collett Cox, later holding posts there as a professor (attested 2017) and faculty member (attested 2026).

Timothy Lubin is an Indology and religious studies scholar. He earned his BA and PhD from Columbia University and an MTS from Harvard University. After lecturing at Harvard and the University of Virginia, he became a professor at Washington and Lee University in 1997.
Tina Rasmussen is a researcher in Buddhist studies and religious studies. She studied under traditional teacher Pa-Auk Sayadaw as well as under MA supervisor Christian K. Wedemeyer.

Tinatin Aleksandrovna Chavchavadze (1928–1997) was a scholar in Iranian and Central Asian studies, Indology, and linguistics. Educated at Tbilisi State University, she taught there and worked at the Giorgi Tsereteli Institute and the Russian Academy of Sciences.

Tine Van Overberghe specializes in Indology and religious studies. She earned a bachelor's degree from Ghent University (2015–2020) and became a PhD student and assistante diplômée at the University of Lausanne.

Tine Vekemans is an Indologist and religious studies scholar. She earned an MA in Oriental Languages and Cultures from Ghent University (2003–2007) and serves there as the Ācārya Mahāprajña Chair for Jain Studies (attested 2026).

Tirtha Halder is a scholar in Indology and philosophy. He completed degrees at the University of Gour Banga, Jadavpur University, and Visva-Bharati University, before pursuing a PhD in Sanskrit at Jawaharlal Nehru University in 2022.

Tirumalai Krishnamacharya (1888–1989) worked in Indology and philosophy. He studied at Queen's College, Benares, and the University of Mysore, and under Ramamohana Brahmachari. He taught at Maharaja's Sanskrit College, Mysore (1931) and Ramakrishna Mission Vivekananda College (~1952).

Tissa Rajapatirana (1933–2021) was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar. He completed his PhD at the Australian National University under Jan Willem de Jong and later served in ANU's Department of South Asian and Buddhist Studies (attested 1988).

Tista Biswas is a scholar of Indology who studied under doctoral supervisor Subuddhi Charan Goswami. She holds a post as the Sir William Jones Research Fellow in Sanskritic Studies at The Asiatic Society (attested 2026).

Tiziana Pontillo is a scholar of Indology and linguistics. She earned a PhD in historical linguistics and philology from the University of Milan (1996–2000) and was appointed Full Professor of Sanskrit Language and Literature at the University of Cagliari in 2022.
Todar Mall was an Indology scholar who studied under Hermann Jacobi and Arthur Anthony Macdonell.
Todd A. Gibson is a scholar in Tibetology and religious studies. He studied under György Kara and earned a PhD from Indiana University Bloomington (attested 1991).

Todd Thornton Lewis works in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He studied at Columbia University under faculty including Alex Wayman and Theodore Riccardi Jr. He holds a professorship at the College of the Holy Cross (attested 1996, 2016–2017).

Tokan Tada (1890–1967) worked in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. After studying at Sera Monastery (1913–1923), he held posts at the University of Tokyo (1924), Tohoku University (1925), and Toyo Bunko (1956).
